title: Darius I
summary: King of Persia, son of Hystaspes (Herodotus 3.88 – 7.4).
description: Added from the Herodotus import (The Histories, tr. Rawlinson). Herodotus gives reign lengths and synchronisms, not BC years, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Herodotus is display-only and gives none).

birth.note: pending CFAH reference (no CFAH anchor point or Table 1 entry found for this)

birth.date: “his eldest son, Darius, was at that time scarce twenty years old”
birth.citation: Herodotus, Histories 1.209 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 93 (PDF p. 95)
birth.note: Darius's age at the time of Cyrus's last campaign. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): Cyrus's death 531/530 BC (see 1.214) + about 20 years gives a birth about 551/550 BC (approximate).

death.note: pending CFAH reference (no CFAH anchor point or Table 1 entry found for this)

death.date: “He died in the year following the revolt of Egypt and the matters here related, after having reigned in all six-and-thirty years”
death.citation: Herodotus, Histories 7.4 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 428 (PDF p. 430)
death.note: DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): Death about 486/485 BC; accession 36 years earlier, about 522/521 BC. Chain from CFAH AP-13 (Xerxes invades Greece, 480 BC): the host wintered at Sardis and marched "on the first approach of spring" (7.37), having set out "at the close of the fifth year" from the recovery of Egypt (7.20), so Egypt was recovered about 485/484 BC; that was "the year following the death of Darius" (7.7), so Darius died about 486/485 BC; he died "in the year following the revolt of Egypt" (7.4), about 487/486 BC, and the revolt came "in the fourth year" after the news of Marathon (7.1), so Marathon was about 490 BC (±1). Agrees with Generations: Darius 522 BC (+ 36 = 486) and the 1st ed. of Preparing (Xerxes 486–465 BC). CONFLICT with the 2nd ed. of Preparing, which dates Xerxes 496–475 BC (the provisional sort of reign-of-xerxes-i), 10 years earlier than Darius's 36 years from 522 allow.

reign.note: From the book's "Ancient Empires" pages (credited in an image to Daily Bible Study, keyway.ca). Same table (read from the page image).

reign.date: “Thus was Darius, son of Hystaspes, appointed king”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 3.88 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 216 (PDF p. 218)
reign.note: DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): about 523/522 BC (Cambyses's death) + 7 months = about 522 BC (anchor CFAH AP-7). Consistent with Generations 522 BC (provisional).

reign.date: “when a year and seven months had passed”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 3.152 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 242 (PDF p. 244)

reign.date: “Thus was Babylon taken for the second time.”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 3.159 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 245 (PDF p. 247)
reign.note: Darius takes Babylon by Zopyrus's stratagem (the first taking was by Cyrus, 1.191).

reign.date: “King Darius received tidings of the taking and burning of Sardis by the Athenians and Ionians”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 5.105 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 364 (PDF p. 366)
reign.note: Synchronism: the burning of Sardis falls in Darius's reign; it is his grievance against Athens.

reign.date: “The next spring Darius superseded all the other generals, and sent down Mardonius”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 6.43 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 385 (PDF p. 387)
reign.note: Mardonius's expedition, the first after the revolt.

reign.date: “For in the three following generations of Darius the son of Hystaspes, Xerxes the son of Darius, and Artaxerxes the son of Xerxes, more woes befell Greece than in the twenty generations preceding Darius”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 6.98 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 408 (PDF p. 410)
reign.note: Said of the Delos earthquake as Datis's fleet sailed for Eretria and Marathon. Herodotus counts the Persian kings to Artaxerxes, son of Xerxes.

reign.date: “all Asia was in commotion by the space of three years”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 7.1 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 426 (PDF p. 428)
reign.note: Darius prepares a second expedition after the news of Marathon. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): About 490 BC for Marathon. Chain from CFAH AP-13 (Xerxes invades Greece, 480 BC): the host wintered at Sardis and marched "on the first approach of spring" (7.37), having set out "at the close of the fifth year" from the recovery of Egypt (7.20), so Egypt was recovered about 485/484 BC; that was "the year following the death of Darius" (7.7), so Darius died about 486/485 BC; he died "in the year following the revolt of Egypt" (7.4), about 487/486 BC, and the revolt came "in the fourth year" after the news of Marathon (7.1), so Marathon was about 490 BC (±1). Consistent with Generations 490 BC (provisional).

reign.date: “in the fourth year, the Egyptians whom Cambyses had enslaved revolted from the Persians”
